text:
Nikita Zadorov's month has been loud. He opened the Bruins' Nov. 8 game against Florida by dropping the gloves with Brady Tkachuk off the opening faceoff, a night that ended with 126 penalty minutes. He told reporters afterward, in a headline carried by NDTV Sports, "I Thought We Could Get Momentum From That." Boston won that one 4-1. It has lost three straight since.

On the ice he's what the 6-foot-7 defenseman has been for most of 804 career games before this season: about 19 minutes a night, a lot of contact (56 hits, 28 blocks) and very little shooting. He has 7 assists and no goals, and his expected goals total of 1.0 says the zero isn't a fluke so much as a style. The encouraging part is the five-on-five share of chances, 54.7% with him on the ice, better than the team without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him slightly above the middle of NHL defensemen last season, and warned that some of his value came from hot shooting around him. For Boston, the question this week is less about Zadorov than whether the team in front of him can stop the slide.
